correctness.rationale: For every compactly supported invariant probability measure, invariance of test functions of \(z\) gives \(\mathbb E[xy\mid z]=bz\). Invariance of \((x^2+y^2)/2\), followed by completing the square, gives exactly \(\mathbb E[(\sqrt a\,x-y)^2]=b(c-(2\sqrt a-a))\mathbb E[z]\). Below \(c_*=2\sqrt a-a\) the resulting quadratic dissipation is positive definite, forcing \((x,y)\to0\) and then \(z\to0\). At equality, zero defect forces support into \(y=\sqrt a\,x\); tangency and the \(z\)-equation reduce compact invariant support to the origin and the two stated equilibria. Above threshold, the same support/tangency argument rules out zero defect for any nonorigin compact invariant measure. The exact rational verifier was inspected and the key identities were independently reconstructed.

value.rationale: The result turns a known local equilibrium/bifurcation threshold into a sharp global recurrence boundary and an exact stationary law for every compact invariant measure, including complete threshold rigidity. That is a natural structural statement about a canonical chaotic flow, not a recomputation of a local Jacobian or an arbitrary parameter slice.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns compact recurrence/invariant measures; it does not classify all unbounded trajectories above threshold.

final_claim: For the Qi system \(\dot x=a(y-x)+yz\), \(\dot y=cx-y-xz\), \(\dot z=xy-bz\) with \(0<a<1\), \(b>0\), the value \(c_*=2\sqrt a-a\) is the exact threshold for nonorigin compact recurrence. Every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[xy\mid z]=bz\) and \(\mathbb E[(\sqrt a\,x-y)^2]=b(c-c_*)\mathbb E[z]\); below threshold all trajectories converge to the origin, at threshold every compact invariant measure is a mixture of the origin and the two stated nonzero equilibria, and above threshold every nonorigin compact invariant measure has strictly positive defect and mean height.
scientific_limitations: The result classifies compact invariant measures and the subthreshold global limit, not all unbounded dynamics above threshold.
